VIEW REPOSITORY

Context

AtlasMatch is being shaped as a practical way for fans to discover host cities and their match-day surroundings.

Problem

The catalog needed a clear, maintainable data model for several connected domain areas without mixing future community features into the current release.

Solution

A modular catalog foundation exposes read-only endpoints for the seeded city, match, hotel, restaurant, transport, and place data.

My contribution

Focused on the backend catalog architecture: cities, matches, hotels, restaurants, transport, places, API design, entity relationships, and Flyway migrations.

Architecture

Spring Boot with JPA and PostgreSQL 17. Flyway owns the schema and seed data; Docker Compose provides a repeatable local stack.

Challenges

Keeping domain relationships, migrations, seed data, and public catalogue responses consistent while preserving room for later features.

Lessons learned

Clear ownership boundaries and migration discipline make a growing product easier to reason about.
